Rashi on Kiddushin 77a:10:1.hebrew: ואין מתחלל - דהא "לא יחלל זרעו" כתיב, ולא את עצמו; דתנן (בכורות דף מה:): "הנושא נשים בעבירה — פסול עד שידור הנאה", וכי הדירה ממנו, עובד עבודה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 77a:10:1.english: And he is not profaned - For "He shall not profane his offspring" is written, and not himself; as we learned in a mishna (Bekhorot 45b): "One who marries women in transgression is disqualified until he vows [to forbid] benefit"; and once he has forbidden her [benefit] from him, he performs the [Temple] service.

Rashi on Kiddushin 77a:10:2.hebrew: מה להוא שאין מתחלל בכ"מ - אפילו בא על השפחה ועל הזונה. תאמר באשה שנפסלת בכ"מ, שאם בא עליה כותי, חלל, נתין, ממזר — פסולה, כדאמרינן לעיל (קידושין דף עד:), ונפקא לן ביבמות (דף סח.) מן "ובת כהן כי תהיה לאיש זר" — כיון שנבעלה לפסול לה, פסלה. והואיל ונפסלת בשאר ביאות איסור, תיפסל אף כאן:
Rashi on Kiddushin 77a:10:2.english: What [is notable] about him, that he is not profaned in any case - Even [if] he engaged in intercourse with a maidservant or with a harlot [he does not become profaned]. Would you say [the same] of a woman, who is disqualified in all cases? For if a Samaritan, a chalal, a Gibeonite, [or] a mamzer engaged in intercourse with her, she is disqualified [from the priesthood], as we say above (Kiddushin 74b), and [as] is derived by us in Yevamot (68a) from [the verse], “And if a priest’s daughter be married unto a stranger” (Leviticus 22:12) — once she has engaged in intercourse with [someone] disqualified to her, he has disqualified her. And since she is disqualified through other forbidden acts of intercourse, let her be disqualified here as well.

Rashi on Kiddushin 77a:11:1.hebrew: ואם נפשך לומר - שום תשובה על ק"ו זה, ותבא להכשירה — הרי לך מקרא מן התורה שהיא מתחללת, דכתיב: "ולא יחלל". עיקר חילול האמור כאן משמע ביאת עצמה, שהיתה כשרה ונתחללה; אבל זרעו מעיקרו הוא נפסל, ואין זה לשון חילול:
Rashi on Kiddushin 77a:11:1.english: And if it is your wish to say - [any] refutation against this a fortiori argument, and you would come to declare her fit — behold, you have a verse from the Torah [teaching] that she is profaned, as it is written: “Neither shall he profane [his offspring]” (Leviticus 21:15). The primary [sense of] profanation stated here indicates the intercourse of [the woman] herself, who was fit and became profaned; but his offspring is disqualified from its inception, and this is not an expression of profanation.

Rashi on Kiddushin 77a:12:1.hebrew: מאי ואם נפשך לומר - מה היה לנו להשיב על ק"ו, דאיצטריך לפרושי קראי:
Rashi on Kiddushin 77a:12:1.english: What is [the meaning of] “And if it is your wish to say”? - What could we have answered against the a fortiori argument, that it was necessary to expound the verses?

Rashi on Kiddushin 77a:12:2.hebrew: הכי קא קשיא ליה - וכי תימא: מעיקרא דדינא, דמייתית היא עצמה מק"ו מזרעו שלא עבר עבירה ונתחללה, איכא למיפרך: מה לזרעו כו':
Rashi on Kiddushin 77a:12:2.english: This is what was difficult to it - And if you would say: At the outset of the argument, where you derive [that] she herself became profaned from an a fortiori [inference] from his offspring who did not commit a transgression, it can be refuted: What about his offspring, etc.?

Rashi on Kiddushin 77a:13:1.hebrew: אי נימא פסולה לו - ואפי' הוא ישראל, אם ביאתו בעבירה שאינו של ממזרת, הוי הולד חלל:
Rashi on Kiddushin 77a:13:1.english: If we say [she is] forbidden to him - And even if he is an Israelite, if his intercourse is through a transgression that is not [one that produces] a mamzer, the offspring is a ḥalal.

Rashi on Kiddushin 77a:13:2.hebrew: והרי מחזיר גרושתו - כשנישאת לאחר, דפסולה, דכתיב (דברים כ״ד:ד׳) לא יוכל בעלה וגו':
Rashi on Kiddushin 77a:13:2.english: And isn’t there [the case of] one who remarries his divorcée - [This refers to a case] where she was married to another [man], for she is forbidden [to him], as it is written (Deuteronomy 24:4): “Her husband... may not [take her again to be his wife].”

Rashi on Kiddushin 77a:13:3.hebrew: ובניה כשרים - בתו כשרה לכהונה, אם ישראל הוא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 77a:13:3.english: And her children are fit - His daughter is fit to [marry into] the priesthood, if he is an Israelite.

Rashi on Kiddushin 77a:13:4.english: “She is an abomination” - That is to say, [she is subject to] the penalty of the transgression.

Rashi on Kiddushin 77a:14:1.hebrew: הכי קא קשיא ליה - וכי תימא: מעיקרא דדינא, דמייתית היא עצמה מק"ו מזרעו שלא עבר עבירה ונתחללה — איכא למיפרך: מה לזרעו, כו':
Rashi on Kiddushin 77a:14:1.english: This is what was difficult for him - And if you were to say: From the outset of the argument, where you derive [the status of] she herself from an a fortiori inference from his offspring — who did not commit a transgression and became profaned — it can be refuted: What [is notable] about his offspring, etc.?

Rashi on Kiddushin 77a:14:2.hebrew: והרי אלמנה - לכ"ג, וגרושה לכהן הדיוט, שמתחללת בביאתו; וכן זונה מביאת פסולין שבא עליה כהן הדיוט, נקראת חללה ללקות עליה משום חללה, דכל איסור כהונה עושה אותה חללה בביאתו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 77a:14:2.english: And behold, a widow - [Forbidden] to a High Priest, and a divorcee to a common priest, who is profaned through his cohabitation; and likewise a zona [who became such] from the cohabitation of disqualified [men], whom a common priest cohabited with, is called a ḥalala [such that one is liable] to receive lashes on her account as a ḥalala, for every priestly prohibition renders her a ḥalala through his cohabitation.

Rashi on Kiddushin 77a:15:2.hebrew: ה"ק איזו היא חללה - המוזכרת בתורה, שעיקרה ממשמעות המקרא, שכתב: "חללה לא יקחו", ואין צריכין לפרש מידי סופרים, דמקרא נפקא בהדיא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 77a:15:2.english: This is what it is saying: Which is the ḥalala - [The one] mentioned in the Torah whose essential [definition is] from the plain meaning of Scripture, which wrote: "[A] ḥalala they shall not take," and it is not necessary to clarify [it] through the Scribes, for it is derived explicitly from Scripture.

Rashi on Kiddushin 77a:15:3.hebrew: כל שנולדה מאיסור כהונה - דסתם חלל היינו ולד פסול לכהונה, מדכתיב: "ולא יחלל זרעו". אבל חללה הנעשית חללה ע"י ביאה, הוצרכו לדרוש בה מקראות, כגון זו שהיתה כשרה ונתחללה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 77a:15:3.english: Any [woman] born from a forbidden priestly [union] - For the ordinary [meaning of] ḥalal is an offspring unfit for the priesthood, as it is written: “He shall not profane his offspring” (Leviticus 21:15). But [regarding] a ḥalalah who becomes a ḥalalah through intercourse — such as one who was fit and became profaned — they needed to expound verses concerning her.

Rashi on Kiddushin 77a:16:1.english: A widow, a widow, a widow - [He] engaged in intercourse with a widow who has three designations of widowhood:

Rashi on Kiddushin 77a:17:1.english: He is liable for only one - [The Gemara] explains it below.

Rashi on Kiddushin 77a:17:2.hebrew: כסדר - כסדר הזה: שנתאלמנה תחילה, ונשאת לשני וגירשה, ונשאת לכהן ונתחללה, ואח"כ נבעלה לאחד מן הפסולים או לקרובים בעילת זנות ונעשית זונה. דמפסולי כהונה חללה איכא, זונה ליכא; ומשאר איסורים זונה הויא, חללה לא הויא, כדלקמן:
Rashi on Kiddushin 77a:17:2.english: In order - In this order: that she was first widowed, and married a second [husband] and he divorced her, and married a priest and became desecrated [a ḥalala], and afterward engaged in intercourse with one of those disqualified [from the congregation] or with [forbidden] relatives in an act of licentious intercourse, and became a zona. For from [intercourse forbidden uniquely to] the priesthood, [the status of] ḥalala applies, [but the status of] zona does not apply; and from other prohibitions she becomes a zona, [while] she does not become a ḥalala, as [explained] below.

Rashi on Kiddushin 77a:17:3.english: She became a zona - [Through intercourse] with [forbidden] relatives or with a mamzer.

Rashi on Kiddushin 77a:17:4.hebrew: ונתחללה - שבא עליה כהן ועשאה חללה, שהיתה אסורה עליו משום זונה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 77a:17:4.english: And became a ḥalala - That a priest engaged in intercourse with her and made her a ḥalala, as she was forbidden to him on account of [being a] zona.

Rashi on Kiddushin 77a:17:5.english: He is liable [for] only one - Below, [the Gemara] explains the reason.

Rashi on Kiddushin 77a:1:1.hebrew: בת חלל זכר - ודוקא נקט, כדקתני ואזיל, דבת חללה שנשאת לישראל כשירה לכהונה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 77a:1:1.english: The daughter of a male ḥalal - And it stated [this] specifically, as it goes on to teach, that the daughter of a ḥalalah who married an Israelite is fit for the priesthood.

Rashi on Kiddushin 77a:1:2.hebrew: לעולם - בת בנו ובת בן בנו, עד סוף כל הדורות של חללים, זכר בן זכר — בת האחרון פסולה כבת הראשון. אבל בת בתו מישראל — כשרה, דלא חמירא בת חלל מחללה, דאמרי': בתה של חללה מישראל כשירה לכהונה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 77a:1:2.english: Forever - The daughter of his son and the daughter of his son's son, until the end of all the generations of ḥalalim — male descendant of a male — the daughter of the last [generation] is unfit like the daughter of the first. But the daughter of his daughter from an Israelite is fit, for the daughter of a ḥalal is no stricter than a ḥalala [herself], as we say: The daughter of a ḥalala from an Israelite is fit for the priesthood.

Rashi on Kiddushin 77a:1:3.hebrew: ישראל שנשא חללה בתו כשירה לכהונה - וטעמא יליף בגמרא. ודוקא ישראל, אבל כהן שנשא חללה — בתו חללה, דכל ולד הנולד בביאת איסור כהונה הוי חלל:
Rashi on Kiddushin 77a:1:3.english: An Israelite who married a ḥalala, his daughter is fit for the priesthood - And the reason is derived in the Gemara. And [this applies] specifically to an Israelite; but [if] a priest married a ḥalala, his daughter is a ḥalala, as any offspring born of an intercourse forbidden to the priesthood is a ḥalal.

Rashi on Kiddushin 77a:1:4.hebrew: חלל שנשא בת ישראל בתו פסולה - בגמ' פריך: הא תנא ליה רישא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 77a:1:4.english: A ḥalal who married an Israelite woman, his daughter is unfit - In the Gemara, it asks: But didn't [the tanna] already teach this in the first clause?

Rashi on Kiddushin 77a:1:5.hebrew: בת גר זכר - ואפילו מישראלית — כבת חלל זכר, ופסולה לכהונה. אבל בת גיורת מישראל — כשירה. וטעמא דכולהו הני תנאי דפליגי בגיורת מפרש בגמ':
Rashi on Kiddushin 77a:1:5.english: The daughter of a male convert - And even [if she was born] of an Israelite woman, [she is] like the daughter of a male ḥalal and disqualified from the priesthood. But the daughter of a female convert from an Israelite [man] is fit [for the priesthood]. And the reasoning of all these Tannaim who disagree regarding a female convert is explained in the Gemara:

Rashi on Kiddushin 77a:2:1.hebrew: ר' אליעזר בן יעקב אומר כו' - לית ליה האי דינא דלקמן (קידושין דף עח.): צד השוה דשאינו ברוב קהל לא פריך — דהיינו דומיא דשיש בהן צד חמור ואין חומר שלהם שוה, ואיכא למ"ד בעלמא (מכות דף ד:): צד חמור לא פריך. ומיהו, גר שנשא גיורת — בתו פסולה, דבעי' מזרע בית ישראל, כדמפרש בגמרא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 77a:2:1.english: Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya’akov says, etc. - He does not accept this derivation [brought] below (Kiddushin 78a), [namely, that regarding] the common denominator of "not being in the majority of the congregation" one cannot refute [it] — which is analogous to [cases] where they have a stringent aspect but their stringencies are not identical, and there is an authority elsewhere (Makkot 4b) [who holds that] a stringent aspect does not refute [a derivation]. However, [in the case of] a male convert who married a female convert, his daughter is unfit, as we require [her to be] "of the seed of the house of Israel," as is explained in the Gemara.

Rashi on Kiddushin 77a:3:1.hebrew: מה להלן - לענין טומאה, הזכרים הוזהרו עליה ולא נקבות, דכתיב: "בני אהרן" — ולא בנות אהרן:
Rashi on Kiddushin 77a:3:1.english: Just as there - With regard to [corpse] impurity, the males were cautioned against it and not females, as it is written: “The sons of Aaron” (Leviticus 21:1) — and not the daughters of Aaron.

Rashi on Kiddushin 77a:3:2.hebrew: אף - בפסולי חללות, זכרים נפסלו ולא נקבות:
Rashi on Kiddushin 77a:3:2.english: So too - Regarding the disqualifications of chalal status, males were disqualified, but not females.

Rashi on Kiddushin 77a:4:1.hebrew: מה להלן - לענין טומאה, הזכרים הוזהרו עליה ולא נקבות, דכתיב: "בני אהרן" — ולא בנות אהרן:
Rashi on Kiddushin 77a:4:1.english: Just as there - With regard to [ritual] impurity, males were cautioned against it and not females, as it is written: "The sons of Aaron" — and not the daughters of Aaron.

Rashi on Kiddushin 77a:4:2.hebrew: אף - בפסולי חללות, זכרים נפסלו ולא נקבות:
Rashi on Kiddushin 77a:4:2.english: So too - With regard to the disqualification of profaned status, males are disqualified, and not females.

Rashi on Kiddushin 77a:5:1.hebrew: בתו של כ"ג - מן האלמנה תישתרי, דהא אמרי' נקבות מותרות:
Rashi on Kiddushin 77a:5:1.english: The daughter of a High Priest - [born] from the widow should be permitted, for we say that females are permitted.

Rashi on Kiddushin 77a:5:2.hebrew: זרעו כתיב - ואפי' נקבות. וכי אהני גזירה שוה — לבת בתו אהני:
Rashi on Kiddushin 77a:5:2.english: “His offspring” is written - And [this includes] even females. And where the verbal analogy is effective, it is effective for his daughter’s daughter.

Rashi on Kiddushin 77a:6:1.hebrew: בת בנו - חלל, תישתרי — דתהני ליה גזירה שוה, ולא אפיק קרא אלא זרעו, אבל זרע זרעו תכשר בנקבות מג"ש:
Rashi on Kiddushin 77a:6:1.english: The daughter of his son - [Who is] a ḥalal, should be permitted — so that the verbal analogy should benefit him; and the verse excluded only his [direct] offspring, but the offspring of his offspring should be fit in [the case of] females from the verbal analogy.

Rashi on Kiddushin 77a:6:2.hebrew: זרעו - האב והזרע הוזכרו בתיבה זו, והיינו הקישא:
Rashi on Kiddushin 77a:6:2.english: His offspring - The father and the offspring are mentioned in this word, and that is the juxtaposition:

Rashi on Kiddushin 77a:6:3.english: The daughter of his daughter - [who is a] ḥalala should be prohibited from this analogy:

Rashi on Kiddushin 77a:8:1.hebrew: כשם שבני ישראל מקוה טהרה לחללות - להכשיר את בתה ממנו לכהונה, כך בנות ישראל מקוה טהרה לחללים — להכשיר את בתו ממנו לכהונה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 77a:8:1.english: Just as the sons of Israel are a ritual bath of purity for ḥalalot - To qualify her daughter from him for the priesthood; so the daughters of Israel are a ritual bath of purity for ḥalalim — to qualify his daughter from him for the priesthood.

Rashi on Kiddushin 77a:8:2.hebrew: בעמיו - מדלא כתיב בעממיו, משמע שאין זרעו מחלל את בתו אלא כשהוא ואשתו מעם אחד, ששניהם חללים:
Rashi on Kiddushin 77a:8:2.english: Among his people - Since it is not written “among his peoples” [be’amamav], it implies that his offspring does not profane his daughter unless he and his wife are of one people, in that both of them are ḥalalim.

Rashi on Kiddushin 77a:9:1.hebrew: היא עצמה מנין - שהאלמנה מתחללת בביאתו מן התרומה ומן הכהונה, ללקות כהן הדיוט הבא עליה אחריו משום חללה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 77a:9:1.english: From where [do we derive that] she herself [is profaned] - That the widow becomes profaned through his intercourse [and disqualified] from [eating] terumah and from [marrying into] the priesthood, so that an ordinary priest who has relations with her after him incurs lashes on account of [her being] a ḥalalah.

Rashi on Kiddushin 77a:9:2.hebrew: היא שעברה עבירה - דכתיב "לא יקחו", להזהיר אשה על ידי האיש, ביבמות בפ' יש מותרות (יבמות דף פד:):
Rashi on Kiddushin 77a:9:2.english: She, who committed a transgression - For it is written: “They shall not take” (Leviticus 21:7), to admonish the woman through the man, [as taught] in Yevamot in the chapter [entitled] Yesh Mutarot (Yevamot 84b).

Tosafot on Kiddushin 77a:12:1.hebrew: [וכ"ת איכא למיפרך מה לזרעו שכן יצירתו בעבירה כו' - תימה: אמאי לא אמרינן נבעלה לפסול לה יוכיח, שאין יצירתה בעבירה ופסול? ואי פרכת: מה לנבעלה לפסול לה, שכן זר אצלה מעיקרא? זרעו יוכיח! וחזר הדין וכו'. ושמא אין כאן צד השוה, או יש שום פירכא. ת"י]:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 77a:12:1.english: [“And if you would say that it can be refuted: What about his offspring, in that his formation is through a transgression, etc.”] - It is puzzling: Why do we not say: [The case of a woman who] had relations with [a man] disqualified for her shall prove [it], as her formation was not through a transgression, and [yet she is] disqualified? And if you refute [this]: What [is notable] about [a woman who] had relations with [a man] disqualified for her? That he is an outsider to her from the outset! [Then] his offspring shall prove [it]! And the argument goes in a circle, etc. And perhaps there is no [valid] common factor here, or there is some refutation. — Tosafot Yeshanim]:
